attempts.summary: On node1, set up /srv/data as a btrfs subvolume (backed by a loop-mounted image at /var/lib/snapshots/srv-data.img, persisted via /etc/fstab) since no snapshot-capable filesystem or spare block device existed. Populated it with sample application data, took a read-only baseline snapshot (btrfs subvolume snapshot -r), then modified /srv/data (edited files, added an unauthorized file, deleted a log). Restored /srv/data to the exact baseline content by deleting the modified subvolume and recreating it from the read-only snapshot, verified via SHA-256 checksums that the restored content matches the baseline byte-for-byte and the tampered file is gone. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id and data checksums pre-restart, issued a native reboot, polled until node1 exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed, and confirmed the btrfs mounts, subvolumes, and file checksums all recovered identically to the pre-restart/baseline state after boot.
